issues.description: fsm-complement produces incorrect results for incomplete DFAs. Since nfa->dfa and fsm-minimize omit transitions to the dead state, the resulting DFA is incomplete. Complementing it without adding these transitions means the complemented FSM still won't accept strings that should lead to the dead state (and thus be accepted by the complement).
issues.code_snippet:
(define (fsm-complement dfa)
  (let* ([m (if (fsm-deterministic? dfa) dfa (nfa->dfa dfa))]
         [non-accepting (filter (lambda (s) (not (member s (fsm-accepting m))))
                                (fsm-states m))])
        (make-fsm (fsm-states m) (fsm-alphabet m) (fsm-transitions m)
                  (fsm-start m) non-accepting)))
issues.suggested_fix: Ensure the DFA is complete before complementing. Add an explicit 'dead' state and transitions to it for all symbols in the alphabet that are missing from the original transitions, then complement by swapping all states.

issues.description: The run-reader implementation of reader-local fails to restore the original environment after the scoped computation. Because the continuation (k '()) of the reader-local effect typically contains the entire rest of the computation (due to monadic bind), recursing with (f env) causes all subsequent operations in the chain to use the modified environment instead of only the intended sub-computation.
issues.suggested_fix: The reader-local effect should carry its sub-computation as part of the payload (similar to writer-listen), or run-reader should be structured to restore the environment after running the sub-computation by calling (k result) with the original env.

issues.description: many-till is susceptible to infinite loops if the body parser p succeeds without consuming any input (e.g., an empty match or parser-pure). Unlike the many combinator, many-till lacks progress checking to break the loop when no input is consumed.
issues.code_snippet:
(define (many-till p end)
  (parser-or (parser-then end (parser-pure '()))
             (parser-bind p (lambda (x)
                                    (parser-bind (many-till p end)
                                                 (lambda (xs)
                                                         (parser-pure (cons x xs))))))))
issues.suggested_fix: Implement progress checking in many-till similar to the many combinator by comparing the state's offset before and after running parser p, and breaking the loop if no progress is made.

issues.description: moore-run and mealy-run incorrectly handle non-deterministic FSMs by arbitrarily taking the first state in the resulting state set (car new-states). This leads to non-deterministic or incorrect output sequences if multiple states are active in an NFA or epsilon-NFA.
issues.suggested_fix: Either restrict Moore and Mealy machines to deterministic FSMs (DFA) or implement a well-defined strategy for handling multiple active states (e.g., returning a set of outputs).

issues.description: run-nondet fails with an error on unknown effects, which breaks effect composition. Most other handlers in this library correctly re-emit unknown effects to allow them to be handled by outer interpreters.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the else case to re-emit the effect using make-eff-op, consistent with other effect handlers like run-state and run-writer.
